image_description: Three Nile crocodiles resting on a sandy bank. The top crocodile has its mouth wide open, displaying teeth and the interior of the mouth. The bottom-left crocodile also has its mouth open but less widely. The bottom-right crocodile has its mouth closed. All exhibit rough, armored skin with visible scutes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snouts are clearly V-shaped and taper towards the nose, distinct from the U-shape of alligators. The head shape is consistent with Crocodylus niloticus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The prompt specifies 'when mouth is closed'. Two subjects have mouths open. One subject (bottom right) has mouth closed, but the angle and resolution make it difficult to definitively verify the 'interlocking' nature or count of teeth in that specific static view. However, the visible teeth in the open mouths are conical and numerous.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eyes are clearly on top of the head. Vertical slit pupils are visible in the bottom-left subject. Nictitating membrane is not clearly deployed/visible, but the eye structure is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are visible at the distal end of the snout on all subjects.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies are long and covered in heavy armor plating.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture shows distinct, raised rectangular scutes arranged in rows along the back and tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration is greyish-brown with high-frequency texture detail consistent with osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodiles are viewed from a dorsal/lateral angle; the belly (ventral surface) is occluded by the ground and body position.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are largely tucked under the body or obscured by sand/other crocodiles. Feet and digit counts are not clearly visible for verification.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail of the top crocodile is visible, showing lateral compression and muscular thickness consistent with the species.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The pink tissue inside the mouth appears slightly overly smooth and plastic-like compared to the hyper-detailed exterior scales, lacking the subtle vascular texture expected in high-res macro photography, though not structurally impossible.

The teeth on the lower jaw of the bottom-left crocodile appear to merge slightly with the gum line without distinct individual roots or separation, looking somewhat 'melted' into the jawbone rather than sitting in sockets.

To rigorously inspect the suspected texture anomalies in the mouth and potential melting in the teeth/gum interface.
To verify that the complex scale patterns are topologically continuous and not generated as disconnected floating textures.
To ensure the overlapping crocodiles have correct depth ordering and no spatial bleeding between bodies.

focus_areas: Integrity of teeth and gum lines (checking for melting/fusion)
Texture consistency of oral cavity vs external skin
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the teeth of the bottom-left crocodile; AI often struggles with the individual separation of teeth in open-mouth poses, leading to fusion artifacts. Also, verify if the 'smoothness' of the mouth interior is an artifact or just a lighting effect.
